newsitem.title: USA: Associated, First Financial to merge.
newsitem.headline: Associated, First Financial to merge.

text.p: Associated Banc-Corp and First Financial Corp said Wednesday they had definitively agreed to merge in a tax-free stock pact exchanging each share of First Financial for 0.765 shares of Associated.
They said the market value of the combined companies would be about $2 billion, based on Tuesday's closing price for Associated Banc-Corp.
Associated shares closed down 1/2 Wednesday at 37-3/4.
First Financial shares closed up 1/8 at 27-1/2.
The deal is expected to be earnings accretive in fiscal 1998, but will result in a one-time charge and one-time accounting adjustments of at least $40 million, net of taxes, the companies said.
Pre-tax savings should be about $10 million in 1998, with savings increasing in future years, they said.

The companies said merger, which has been approved by both their boards, will be handled as a pooling of interests. The pact requires shareholder approval from both companies, but is expected to close late in 1997.

The companies said the merged institution will have combined assets of $10.5 billion, equity capital of about $900 million and over 220 full-service banking locations throughout Wisconsin and Illinois.

Associated chief executive H.B. Conlon will be chairman and chief executive of the combined companies. John Seramur, First Financial's chief executive, will be named vice chairman and remain president of First Financial during the integration period.
The board of the combined company will have seven of the existing directors from each company.
The companies said they both executed a stock option pact providing for the purchase of 19.9 percent of each other's common stock.
The merged company will retain the Associated Banc-Corp name and have its headquarters in Green Bay, Wisconsin.
